newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Moderate quakes rock north, central Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Moderate quakes rock north, central Philippines.

text.p: Three moderate earthquakes rocked parts of central and northern Philippines on Wednesday, but there were no reports of casualties or damage, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) said.

Ric Mangao, a scientist at the Phivolcs seismology division, said the country had been registering an increased number of quakes in the past two weeks, but said this was normal in a country sitting on several major geological faults.
"We sometimes record heightened seismic activities, but this will die down after one or two weeks ... It's normal," Mangao told Reuters.
The Philippines registers five quakes every day, most of which are too weak to be felt.
The first quake occurred shortly after midnight (1600 GMT Tuesday) with a magnitude of 4.7 on the Richter scale. It was felt in central Leyte island.
The second, with a magnitude of six and reported earlier on Wednesday, was registered at 2.07 a.m. and was centred 40 km northeast of Laoag city, the capital of the northern Ilocos Norte province.
The third quake, at 6.10 a.m., measured four on the Richter scale and centred 66 km (41 miles) northeast of the northernmost island of Batanes.
